claims.claim: No contemporary inscription names who built the Sphinx
claims.quote: there is not one single contemporary inscription which connects the Sphinx with Khafre

claims.claim: Archaeological evidence points to the reign of Khufu or Khafre, c.2600–2500 BC
claims.quote: The archaeological evidence suggests the Great Sphinx was created between 2600 and 2500 BC for the king Khufu, the builder of the Great Pyramid of Giza, or his son Khafre, the builder of the second Pyramid at Giza.

claims.claim: Card 1 image is by Maison Bonfils, Egypt, c.1867–1899, public domain
claims.quote: Author: Maison Bonfils (Beirut, Lebanon), photographers : Félix (1831-1885), his wife, Lydie (1837-1918) and his son, Adrien (1861-1929)

claims.claim: Chisel/rod marks show the nose was pried off
claims.quote: Examination of the Sphinx's face shows marks made by long rods or chisels hammered into the face: one at the bridge of the nose, and another below the nostril. The nose was apparently then pried off

claims.claim: Frederic Louis Norden drew the Sphinx noseless in 1737, over 60 years before Napoleon's arrival
claims.quote: However, drawings made by Frederic Louis Norden in 1737 show the Sphinx's nose missing, over 60 years before Napoleon's arrival.

claims.claim: Al-Maqrizi blamed a Sufi iconoclast, Muhammad Sa'im al-Dahr, in 1378
claims.quote: Writing in the early 15th century, Arab historian al-Maqrīzī attributed the loss of the nose to Muhammad Sa'im al-Dahr, a Sufi Muslim from the khanqah of Sa'id al-Su'ada in 1378.

claims.claim: For about 300 years Europeans depicted the Sphinx with a woman's face
claims.quote: From the 16th to the 19th centuries, European observers described the Sphinx having the face, neck and breast of a woman.

claims.claim: George Sandys (1615) called the Sphinx a harlot
claims.quote: George Sandys stated the Sphinx was a harlot

claims.claim: Other European depictions gave the Sphinx curly hair, a dog collar, and a hairnet
claims.quote: he, or his artist and engraver, pictured it as a curly-haired monster with a grassy dog collar

claims.claim: Card 3 image comes from George Sandys, A Relation of a Journey, 1615
claims.quote: The  Great Sphinx of Giza  in  George Sandys ,  A relation of a journey begun an dom. 1610  (1615)

claims.claim: The stele lines naming the builder ("Khaf") flaked off and were destroyed
claims.quote: When the stele was re-excavated in 1925, the lines of text referring to Khaf had flaked off and were destroyed.

claims.claim: Thutmose IV erected the stele between the Sphinx's paws c.1400 BC
claims.quote: The first documented attempt at an excavation dates to c. 1400 BC, when the young Thutmose IV (1401–1391 or 1397–1388 BC) gathered a team and, after much effort, managed to dig out the front paws, between which he erected a shrine housing the Dream Stele, an inscribed granite slab

claims.claim: The space between the paws was found to be thirty-five feet long
claims.quote: the space between the paws was found to be thirty-five feet long and ten feet wide

claims.claim: Caviglia uncovered the Sphinx's chest in 1817
claims.quote: In 1817, the first modern archaeological dig, supervised by the Italian Giovanni Battista Caviglia, uncovered the Sphinx's chest completely.

claims.claim: By 1887 the paws, altar and flights of steps were clear of sand
claims.quote: In the beginning of the year 1887, the chest, the paws, the altar, and plateau were all made visible. Flights of steps were unearthed

claims.claim: The original Egyptian name of the Sphinx is unknown
claims.quote: The original name the Old Kingdom creators gave the Sphinx is unknown

claims.claim: Who removed the nose remains unproven
claims.quote: The circumstances of the destruction of the Sphinx's nose are unknown, but examinations of the face have shown evidence of a deliberate act with rods or chisels.

claims.claim: Khufu reigned c.2590–2566 BC
claims.quote: during the reign of Khufu (c. 2590–2566 BC) or Khafre (c. 2558–2532 BC)

claims.claim: Khafre was Khufu's son and reigned c.2558–2532 BC
claims.quote: or his son Khafre, the builder of the second Pyramid at Giza

claims.claim: Scholars have also argued the Sphinx was the work of Djedefre
claims.quote: In 2004, Vassil Dobrev of the Institut Français d'Archéologie Orientale in Cairo announced he had uncovered new evidence the Great Sphinx may have been the work of the little-known pharaoh Djedefre (2528–2520 BC)

claims.claim: Selim Hassan excavated the Sphinx enclosure and wrote in 1949
claims.quote: Selim Hassan, writing in 1949 on recent excavations of the Sphinx enclosure, makes note of this circumstance

claims.claim: The name "Sphinx" is Greek and was applied around 2,000 years after its construction
claims.quote: The commonly used name "Sphinx" was given to it in classical antiquity, around 2,000 years after the commonly accepted date of its construction by reference to a Greek mythological beast

claims.claim: The nose was not destroyed by cannonfire from Napoleon's troops
claims.quote: Contrary to a popular myth, the nose was not destroyed by cannonfire from Napoleon's troops during his 1798 Egyptian campaign.

claims.claim: Sa'im al-Dahr acted after seeing local peasants making offerings to the Sphinx
claims.quote: According to al-Maqrīzī, Sa'im al-Dahr saw local peasants making offerings to the Sphinx in the hope of increasing their harvest and defaced the Sphinx in an act of iconoclasm.

claims.claim: The Sphinx was buried by sand repeatedly over its history
claims.quote: Some time around the First Intermediate Period, the Giza Necropolis was abandoned, and drifting sand eventually buried the Sphinx up to its shoulders.

claims.claim: The stele's text was already damaged and incomplete when it was discovered
claims.quote: When the stele was discovered, its lines of text were already damaged and incomplete.

claims.claim: Who the Sphinx's face portrays is still disputed
claims.quote: but a consensus has not been reached and the person(s) in whose likeness the Sphinx was carved remains in dispute
